key_insight: In this open-label, waitlist-controlled trial, two psilocybin doses over two weeks were associated with meaningful short-term reductions in OCD symptoms in participants who had not benefited from prior standard therapies.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest psilocybin could be a potential adjunctive option for treatment-resistant OCD, but the evidence remains preliminary and is not yet practice-changing.
method: 37 adults with OCD were enrolled; 30 completed 1-month follow-up.
Participants received psilocybin 20 mg, then 30 mg if tolerated, under supportive conditions.
Immediate-treatment and waitlist-control groups were compared, with the waitlist group crossing over later.
evidence_signal: Compared with waitlist controls, the immediate-treatment group showed a significant decrease in Y-BOCS scores (F(2,56)=16.17, p<0.001), with improvement persisting one month after the second dose.
watch_item: Open-label design, small sample size, and short follow-up limit causal certainty and generalizability.
paper_title: An Open-Label Multidose Psilocybin Intervention for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
